title: Mesentery, omentum, peritoneum and retroperitoneum

steps.tx: Plain abdominal radiography identifies distinct gas patterns during visceral perforation. **Pneumoperitoneum** on plain radiography demonstrates the **Rigler sign** (visualisation of both the mucosal and serosal sides of the bowel wall outlined by air), the continuous diaphragm sign, and the football sign (large oval gas lucency outlining the falciform ligament in supine infants).
steps.say: Plain abdominal radiography identifies distinct gas patterns during visceral perforation. steps.tx: Bowel wall gas identifies catastrophic transmural injury across cross-sectional studies. **Pneumatosis intestinalis** denotes gas within the bowel wall, benign when associated with pulmonary disease or steroids, but indicating **acute mesenteric ischaemia** and impending bowel necrosis when accompanied by portomesenteric venous gas, bowel wall thickening, or non-enhancing enteric wall mucosa.
steps.say: Bowel wall gas identifies catastrophic transmural injury across cross-sectional studies. steps.tx: Cross-sectional analysis of mesenteric fatty architecture reveals specific reactive inflammatory disorders. **Mesenteric panniculitis** characteristically demonstrates a solitary, well-defined fibrofatty mass in the root of the small bowel mesentery with the **misty mesentery** sign (increased attenuation > -40 HU), fat halo sign (preserved fat ring around mesenteric vessels), and a pseudocapsule, without vascular invasion.

steps.tx: Advanced peritoneal mucinous dissemination demonstrates unique cross-sectional features. **Pseudomyxoma peritonei** typically originates from a ruptured low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN), producing gelatinous ascites that causes characteristic **scalloping of the visceral margins** of the liver and spleen without frank parenchymal invasion, accompanied by omental caking.

steps.tx: Peritoneal implants exhibit distinct spatial predilections governed by fluid dynamics. **Peritoneal carcinomatosis** predominantly implants at sites of physiological peritoneal fluid pooling: the **greater omentum** (omental cake), pouch of Douglas, right paracolic gutter, and ileocaecal junction, most commonly originating from ovarian, gastric, or colorectal adenocarcinoma.

steps.tx: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue masses require precise histopathological differentiation. **Retroperitoneal liposarcoma** is the most common primary retroperitoneal malignancy, characterized by large size (> 10 cm), macroscopic fat density on CT, and thick irregular non-lipomatous soft-tissue septa (> 2 mm), with **dedifferentiated liposarcoma** showing abrupt transitions to high-grade non-lipomatous solid components.
steps.say: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue masses require precise histopathological differentiation. Retroperitoneal liposarcoma is the most common primary retroperitoneal malignancy, characterized by large size over 10 cm, macroscopic fat density on CT, and thick irregular non-lipomatous soft-tissue septa over 2 mm, with dedifferentiated liposarcoma showing abrupt transitions to high-grade non-lipomatous solid components.

steps.tx: Fibro-inflammatory retroperitoneal processes can encase critical retroperitoneal tubes. **Retroperitoneal fibrosis** (Ormond disease) presents as a plaque-like confluent soft-tissue mass centered at the aortic bifurcation (L4-L5), characteristically drawing the **ureters medially** with resultant hydronephrosis, associated with elevated serum IgG4 levels in 50% of cases.

steps.tx: Postoperative peritoneal defects predispose to potentially strangulating bowel herniations. **Internal hernia** through the **mesenteric defect** following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass typically produces the swirl sign (rotation of the superior mesenteric vessels and mesentery) and mushroom sign (herniated loops mushrooming between the mesenteric root and colon).
